To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IgE anti- OKT3 antibodies are only detected in heavily OKT3-sensitized patients, that the fine specificity of these antibodies is mainly anti-idiotypically directed and that, in some patients, an anti-isotype response is also detectable.

(1) anti-OKT 3 IgE Abs appear in about one-third of OKT3-treated recipients, (2) they are mostly anti-idiotypically directed, and (3), they only develop in patients also showing a strong anti-OKT-3 IgG humoral response.
exposure to OKT-3 may lead to the production of IgE antibodies that, however, are detected in only about 3% of the patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fine specificity of IgE anti-drug Abs and their relationship to IgG anti-drug Abs.
the fine specificity of IgE response in OKT-treated patients.
the humoral response in patients undergoing treatment with OKT3, with the aim to better understand the mechanisms of the anaphylactoid reactions occurring in a few cases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the appearance of anti-OKT antibody in patients treated with OKT3 is associated with a risk of anaphylactic reaction.
IgE sensitization to OKT3 is not frequent but, when it occurs, it is usually directed against idiotypic determinants of this monoclonal antibody and is associated with high levels of IgG Abs.
OKT3 treatment may lead to the appearance of specific IgE Abs in a minority of sensitized patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IgE Abs to the monoclonal OKT3 are not frequent and do not appear in all OKT3-treated subjects.
IgE sensitization to OKT3 is not a frequent event, and it appears in patients showing a high degree of sensitization to this monoclonal antibody.
OKT3-induced IgE Abs are not a frequent finding and that their appearance may not be a sufficient criterion to explain the occurrence of anaphylactic reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the IgE response to OKT3 is not a common event, but when it occurs, it is usually associated with high titers of conventional IgG Abs and may be directed to idiotypic and/or isotypic determinations of OKT3.
anti-OKT 3 IgE antibodies may be found in patients with a high titer of IgG anti-idiotypics.
anti-OKT antibodies, including IgE Abs, are only found in heavily sensitized recipients.
